ownership_model.summary: Every execution runs against one Heap; a returned completion value is reclaimable only while that Heap (or a value that pins it) stays live. Caller heap + optional caller global: no exit-time sweep; caller drives Heap::collect. Call-local heap (heap==nullptr, global==nullptr): one final sweep rooted at Completion.value on every exit; a heap-backed completion pins the local heap through js_value::heap so self-referential and mutually reachable returned graphs remain valid and are reclaimed when the value is released. Caller global without caller heap: rejected deterministically before execution.

corrective_review.summary: The candidate repair at 15df113 was reviewed and corrected at d35999f. The corrective model (a) rejects a caller global combined with a call-local heap instead of letting the final sweep lose or mutate externally owned state, and (b) makes self-referential returned values lifetime-safe via heap affinity rather than documenting them as a caller-owned-heap requirement.

notes: Discovery evidence for the pre-fix standalone VM leak is retained as docs/evidence/memory-safety/post-preview-pc0v-vm-valgrind-fail.json plus the raw full log; the leak is not rewritten into a pass.
Intermediate-pass evidence at 15df113 is retained but marked -15df113-superseded; final Valgrind pass evidence is recorded per workload with -pass suffixes at the corrected commit d35999f.

Focused tests cover self-referential objects, arrays, closures and mutually reachable graphs, every exit class (normal, throw, malformed bytecode, instruction budget, stack limit, escaped return), persistent caller globals, and deterministic rejection of a caller global without a caller heap.
PC0V is complete only at the tested JS++ commit d35999f and TSCC commit 1bc3047; PC0P second-platform packaging remains pending.
